name: Samuel Riker
bio: A Representative from New York; born in Newtown, Long Island, N.Y., April 8, 1743; attended the common schools; member of the Newtown, N.Y., committee of correspondence in 1774; was supervisor of Suffolk County, N.Y., in 1783; served in the Revolutionary War, lieutenant of Light Horse; member of the New York state assembly, 1784; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Eighth Congress to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of John Smith (November 5, 1804-March 3, 1805); unsuccessful candidate for re-election to the Ninth Congress in 1804; elected to the Tenth Congress as a Democratic Republican (March 4, 1807-March 3, 1809); died on May 19, 1823, in Newtown, Long Island, N.Y.; interment in the Dutch Reformed Cemetery.
